original_value: This paper presents a Wearable Prototype for indoor mapping developed by the University of Vigo. The system is based on a Velodyne LiDAR, acquiring points with 16 rays for a simplistic or low-density 3D representation of reality. With this, a Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (3D-SLAM) method is developed for the mapping and generation of 3D point clouds of scenarios deprived from GNSS signal. The quality of the system presented is validated through the comparison with a commercial indoor mapping system, Zeb-Revo, from the company GeoSLAM and with a terrestrial LiDAR, Faro Focus3D X330. The first is considered as a relative reference with other mobile systems and is chosen due to its use of the same principle for mapping: SLAM techniques based on Robot Operating System (ROS), while the second is taken as ground-truth for the determination of the final accuracy of the system regarding reality. Results show that the accuracy of the system is mainly determined by the accuracy of the sensor, with little increment in the error introduced by the mapping algorithm.

result.paraphrase: This paper describes a wearable indoor-mapping prototype developed at the University of Vigo. Built around a Velodyne LiDAR with 16 beams, it captures points for a simple, low-density 3D representation of reality. Using this setup, a Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (3D-SLAM) method is developed to map and generate 3D point clouds in environments without GNSS signals. The system’s quality is assessed by comparison with the Zeb-Revo commercial indoor-mapping system from GeoSLAM and with a Faro Focus3D X330 terrestrial LiDAR. The former serves as a relative benchmark against other mobile systems and is selected because it uses the same mapping principle, namely SLAM techniques based on the Robot Operating System (ROS), while the latter is used as ground truth to determine the system’s final accuracy relative to reality. Results indicate that the system’s accuracy is mainly limited by the sensor’s accuracy, with only a small increase in error introduced by the mapping algorithm.
